section_summary: This section moves from the end of an association’s rules into 1937–1938 reports on Japanese fishing abroad. Most documents follow the Japanese-owned AMANO MARU as it obtains provisional Panamanian registry, visits Honolulu and California, and raises concern among Panama Canal defense authorities. Other documents concern Japanese fishing in Hong Kong, proposed study trips for Mexican fishermen, the Alaska salmon dispute, and Japanese fishery law.

subfiles.title: Association rules, concluding pages
subfiles.about: Sets rules for meetings, voting, finances, and the fiscal year.
subfiles.summary: Concluding articles govern general meetings, decisions, minutes, receipts, budgets, and the association’s fiscal year.

subfiles.title: Japanese vessel’s application for Panamanian registry
subfiles.about: Summarizes Yokohama reports on an application to register the AMANO in Panama.
subfiles.summary: Notes that approval of the application was still unknown.

subfiles.title: Japanese attempts to extend fishing activities to Panama
subfiles.about: Forwards the AMANO’s application for Panamanian registry.
subfiles.summary: Boyce encloses the registration application and refers to his earlier report.

subfiles.title: Japanese vessel’s application for Panamanian registry, duplicate
subfiles.about: Duplicates the summary of Yokohama’s registry report.
subfiles.summary: Repeats that approval of the AMANO application was unknown.

subfiles.title: Japanese attempts to extend fishing activities to Panama, duplicate
subfiles.about: Duplicates Boyce’s cover despatch forwarding the application.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a copy of the application for Panamanian registry.

subfiles.title: Application for registration of fishing vessel
subfiles.about: Requests registration of an Amano fishing vessel under construction at Shimizu.
subfiles.summary: Lists ownership, construction, dimensions, engine, equipment, and surveyor.

subfiles.title: Mexican fishermen’s study trip: cross-reference
subfiles.about: Points to a report on Mexican delegates studying Japanese fishing methods.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references file 812.628/392.

subfiles.title: Mexican fishermen invited to study in Japan
subfiles.about: Reports a proposed trip for Mexican fishermen’s cooperative delegates.
subfiles.summary: Mexico’s federal bureau invited cooperatives to send experienced fishermen to Japan aboard Japanese vessels, where they would study fisheries, schools, hatcheries, and methods before instructing their cooperatives at home.

subfiles.title: Japanese activities in the Hong Kong fishing industry
subfiles.about: Reports consolidation of Japanese fishing firms and their dominance of Hong Kong fish supplies.
subfiles.summary: Donovan reports that Nippon Suisan Kaisha absorbed Kyodo Gyogyo Kaisha’s Hong Kong operations. A newspaper account says Japanese trawlers supplied much of Hong Kong’s fish and shipped Hainan catches to the Philippines; local Chinese competitors faced a stronger combine.

subfiles.title: AMANO MARU granted Panamanian registry
subfiles.about: Reports provisional registry and the AMANO MARU’s planned voyage and crew.
subfiles.summary: Panama granted registry, then instructed its consul to seek specific approval before registering other Japanese ships. Boyce reports that the AMANO MARU would sail via Honolulu to San Pedro with a Danish master and a predominantly Japanese officer corps said to include naval reservists.

subfiles.title: AMANO alien crew list
subfiles.about: Identifies the AMANO’s crew, positions, nationalities, and physical descriptions.
subfiles.summary: The two-page manifest names the Danish master and Japanese officers and seamen.

subfiles.title: Request for AMANO crew list
subfiles.about: Requests the crew list and notes Canal defense concern over Japanese-owned fishing vessels.
subfiles.summary: Flexer asks for the enclosed crew list cited by Boyce, praises his reporting, and says Canal defense authorities are disturbed by plans for additional vessels.

subfiles.title: Assistant Secretary routing note
subfiles.about: Contains a brief filing or indexing instruction.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten instruction appears to request indexing.

subfiles.title: Cover note for Alaska salmon investigation
subfiles.to: Mr. Sayre and Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Introduces a report on Japanese fishing prospects in Bristol Bay.
subfiles.summary: Flags Pacific Coast agitation and possible anti-Japanese incidents; directs readers to the report’s conclusions.

subfiles.title: Proposed method of dealing with Japanese participation in Alaska salmon fisheries
subfiles.about: Proposes an interdivisional committee to address the Bristol Bay fishing dispute.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum warns that agitation and threatened cargo boycotts could grow unless the Department acts. It proposes a committee to review evidence, assess policy and further research, and recommend action, while consulting visiting Alaska fishing representatives.

subfiles.title: Japanese fishing company incorporated in Panama
subfiles.about: Examines Amano company ownership and Canal defense objections to a Japanese fishing fleet.
subfiles.summary: Flexer reports intense concern among Canal defense authorities about Japanese-crewed vessels near the Pacific entrance. He details the Panamanian incorporation and resident ownership of the Amano company, complicating proposed restrictions on foreign owners. The despatch reviews registry policy, fishing licenses, American tuna operations, possible processing arrangements, and the company’s uncertain plans.

subfiles.title: Local Joint Board minutes on Japanese fishing vessels
subfiles.about: Records defense officials’ recommendations for preventing Japanese fishing vessels from operating near the Canal.
subfiles.summary: After reviewing Boyce’s April report, the Board calls a Japanese-crewed fleet near the Canal undesirable. It recommends seeking Panamanian restrictions on foreign fishing vessels, examining American crew requirements, and investigating the AMANO’s California connections.

subfiles.title: Correction to Legation despatch
subfiles.about: Corrects a cited despatch date.
subfiles.summary: Changes the date of despatch No. 615 to February 14, 1935.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on AMANO crew list
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Sends a photostatic AMANO crew list and requests further reporting.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the list and requests reports on military, naval, and Panamanian views.

subfiles.title: State Department review of AMANO and Canal defense concerns
subfiles.about: Summarizes registration, ownership, crew, naval reports, and proposed departmental action.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum recounts Panama’s provisional registry and the Local Joint Board’s objections. It notes Yoshitaro Amano’s Panamanian residence, the vessel’s unusually large officer contingent, reported naval reserve links, and its expected fishing for Van Camp. It suggests joint consideration of action.

subfiles.title: Navy Department transmittal of Honolulu report
subfiles.about: Forwards the Fourteenth Naval District’s report on the AMANO.
subfiles.summary: Sends a confidential report concerning the vessel, its company, and personnel.

subfiles.title: Visit of Panamanian motor ship AMANO to Honolulu
subfiles.from: O. C. Murfin, Fourteenth Naval District
subfiles.to: Commandants, Fifteenth and Eleventh Naval Districts
subfiles.about: Documents the AMANO’s Honolulu stop, crew, equipment, and intended fishing route.
subfiles.summary: The report records the vessel’s July 1–2 stop, crew list, technical specifications, radio equipment, and the master’s account. It says Van Camp backed the fuel purchase and that the AMANO planned to fish off San Clemente before proceeding to Panama.

subfiles.title: 111 ton fishing vessel built in Japan here today
subfiles.about: Reports the AMANO MARU’s arrival in Honolulu.
subfiles.summary: Describes construction, cost, company management, and planned tuna fishing in Panama.

subfiles.title: A sign of progress of Marine Products Japan
subfiles.about: Profiles the AMANO MARU, its owners, crew, voyage, and fishing plans.
subfiles.summary: The translated article presents the vessel as a Japanese-built tuna boat for Panama and describes Amano’s enterprise, Shiraishi’s management, ship specifications, and selected crew. It recounts the maiden voyage and quotes Shiraishi on possible future fishing around Hawaii.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Navy report
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the Navy’s report on the AMANO.
subfiles.summary: Thanks the Navy Secretary for the Fourteenth Naval District report.

subfiles.title: Panamanian instructions against further Japanese fishing-vessel registration
subfiles.about: Reports Panama’s cable restricting registration and the AMANO’s six-month provisional certificate.
subfiles.summary: Holmes says Panama intended to refuse permanent registry after the provisional period.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Admiral Holmes
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Holmes’s confidential information on Panamanian registration.
subfiles.summary: Thanks Holmes for forwarding the registry information.

subfiles.title: Seventy-five per cent labor law and Japanese fishing vessels
subfiles.about: Forwards an editorial urging application of Panama’s labor law to the Amano enterprise.
subfiles.summary: Flexer explains that applying the law to foreign-trade vessels would threaten Panama’s registry revenue, while strict application to the AMANO could defeat its fishing enterprise.

subfiles.title: Tuna fishing and the 75-per cent law
subfiles.about: Advocates applying Panamanian labor requirements to Japanese tuna concessionaires.
subfiles.summary: Argues that the labor law should apply equally to the tuna venture.

subfiles.title: Japanese fishery activities in Panama and Mexico
subfiles.about: Reports on the AMANO’s Honolulu visit and an intercepted message from a Japanese vessel in Mexico.
subfiles.summary: Bingham details the AMANO’s ownership, crew, equipment, supply stop, California fishing plans, and Shiraishi’s interest in Hawaiian waters. An intercepted message from the MINO(WA) MARU at Mazatlán is interpreted as suggesting wider Japanese fishing plans involving the Amano company.

subfiles.title: Handwritten departmental routing note
subfiles.about: Contains a largely illegible handwritten comment.
subfiles.summary: A brief, partly unreadable note accompanies the fishing correspondence.

subfiles.title: Japanese fishing activities in Panama
subfiles.about: Reviews AMANO registry, Japanese market fishing, Panamanian policy, and Canal defense concerns.
subfiles.summary: Flexer reports that Panama barred new provisional registrations without approval but had already registered the AMANO. He questions whether its expected permanent-registration refusal has a legal basis, describes the vessel’s California fishing, and recounts Panama’s temporary suspension of Chinese and Japanese ship registrations amid the Sino-Japanese conflict. He also reports concern over Japanese crews in local waters and plans to apply Panama’s labor law, enclosing two newspaper items.

subfiles.title: Bar Sino-Jap ship registry in Panama
subfiles.about: Reports Panama’s provisional suspension of Chinese and Japanese vessel registrations.
subfiles.summary: Links the order to Japanese blockade notices and possible diplomatic conflict.

subfiles.title: What Price Fish?
subfiles.about: Raises espionage concerns about the AMANO MARU near the Panama Canal.
subfiles.summary: Questions Amano’s wealth, ownership structure, vessel equipment, and prospective crew.

subfiles.title: Magdalena Bay AMANO report: cross-reference
subfiles.about: Points to a report on AMANO activity at Magdalena Bay.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references a Special Service Squadron report in file 812.345/33.

subfiles.title: Harry Stuhr and the Bristol Bay salmon dispute
subfiles.about: Records a meeting with an Alaska fisherman concerning possible Japanese fishing and a cargo boycott.
subfiles.summary: Stuhr sought information on State Department action to protect Bristol Bay salmon interests. Officials described continuing work but declined details and warned that a boycott of Japanese freight could hurt the fishermen’s case.

subfiles.title: Japanese fishing vessels arrested near Singapore: cross-reference
subfiles.about: Points to reports of Dutch arrests and firing on Japanese fishing vessels.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes reported incidents in the Riau Archipelago and cites another file.

subfiles.title: Japanese attempts to extend fishing activities in Panama
subfiles.about: Reports a Panamanian-Japanese understanding to deny new registrations to both Chinese and Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Boyce recounts a Panamanian consul’s account of disputes over Chinese ships transferred to Panama’s flag during Japan’s blockade. Panama reportedly agreed to stop registering Chinese vessels if Japanese vessels were also refused; the AMANO MARU’s existing status remained uncertain.

subfiles.title: What Price Fish? (second copy)
subfiles.about: Repeats the editorial questioning the AMANO MARU’s purpose and ownership.
subfiles.summary: Connects the fishing vessel to Canal security fears and Amano’s business interests.

subfiles.title: AMANO provisional registration reportedly extended
subfiles.about: Reports the AMANO’s departure for Costa Rica and a six-month registry extension.
subfiles.summary: The AMANO arrived at Balboa, then sailed for Puntarenas after Panama reportedly extended its provisional registry. Flexer describes divided cabinet views, possible Costa Rican registration, and enclosed translations of Panamanian correspondence on the suspension of Chinese and Japanese vessel registrations.

subfiles.title: Japanese consul’s blockade notice to Panama
subfiles.about: Transmits the Japanese consul’s notice of Japan’s blockade of China’s coast.
subfiles.summary: Lefevre forwards Tetsue Umimoto’s note and a translation of Japan’s notice.

subfiles.title: Suspension of Chinese and Japanese ship registrations
subfiles.about: Reports seizure of a Panamanian-registered former Chinese ship and orders a registration suspension.
subfiles.summary: Lefevre describes the TECHEKN’s capture by Japanese forces and transcribes instructions to Panama’s consul general in Hong Kong to suspend registrations of Chinese and Japanese ships indefinitely.

subfiles.title: Inquiry into AMANO activities in Costa Rica
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests discreet reporting on possible Costa Rican registry and further AMANO activity.
subfiles.summary: Asks the minister at San José to investigate developments after the vessel sailed to Puntarenas.

subfiles.title: Japanese fishery law: cross-reference
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram on aliens’ rights to own or operate fishing vessels in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Notes no express ban, though licenses for aliens appeared doubtful.

subfiles.title: Alien ownership and operation under Japanese fishery law
subfiles.about: Analyzes legal restrictions on alien fishing-vessel ownership, operation, and labor in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The embassy finds no specific statutory bar to aliens owning or operating Japanese fishing vessels in coastal waters or on the high seas. It cautions that required fishing and labor licenses may be withheld or canceled, and that subsidies are restricted to Japanese vessels.

subfiles.title: Japanese fishing and cotton activities in Costa Rica: cross-reference
subfiles.about: Points to an investigation of Japanese fishing and cotton projects around Puntarenas.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Second Secretary Collins’s investigation in file 818.628/64.
